name: Meta Richland Parish data center (Hyperion)
summary: Meta campus on the former Franklin Farm megasite in Richland Parish, northeast Louisiana, built to house Hyperion, which Meta calls its largest AI cluster. Announced in December 2024 as a USD 10 billion project, it was placed in late 2025 in a joint venture 80% owned by Blue Owl-managed funds and expanded in July 2026 to a planned 5 GW of IT capacity and more than USD 50 billion of investment. Entergy Louisiana is adding gas-fired generation, batteries and transmission upgrades to serve the site under a 20-year agreement. Construction began in December 2024, and officials expect full build-out around 2036.

location.note: Sources place the campus on the former Franklin Farm megasite between Rayville and Delhi; the 2026 state release is datelined Holly Ridge and WRKF refers to the Holly Ridge site. Coordinates are the Holly Ridge community point from OpenStreetMap Nominatim, not a surveyed site boundary.

milestones.note: The state said site work would begin in December; later reporting dates the groundbreaking to December 2024.
The Louisiana Public Service Commission voted 4-1 to approve Entergy Louisiana's three new gas plants tied to the campus, as reported on 2025-08-20.
Meta announced the joint venture with Blue Owl-managed funds at the end of October 2025 and on 21 October cited a development cost of about USD 27 billion.
Expansion to 5 GW of IT capacity and more than USD 50 billion of investment.
Target for roughly 2 GW of initial capacity, as reported before the 2026 expansion.
Officials expect the full build-out of both phases by 2036.

power_sources.description: Supplied by Entergy Louisiana under a 20-year agreement. Regulators approved three new combined-cycle gas units in 2025 (two in Richland Parish, one at Waterford) along with transmission upgrades; the 2026 state release refers to seven new gas plants, while WRKF reports Entergy sought approval for ten. These are utility plants rather than on-site generation.
Three grid-scale battery systems are part of the Entergy arrangement announced with the 2026 expansion.
The 2026 arrangement includes possible nuclear development, including an output increase at Entergy's Waterford 3 plant.

Entergy was cleared to fast-track up to 1,500 MW of solar; Meta earlier pledged to help bring at least 1,500 MW of new renewables to the grid and in 2026 committed to fund up to 2.5 GW of clean energy.
